lyrics:
[Intro: slow acoustic guitar, vinyl crackle, deep kick]

[Chorus: sung, laid-back, nostalgic]
It's blacktop now where the dust used to rise
Streetlights shining where we counted fireflies
There's a cul-de-sac sitting on our fishing hole
They smoothed it all over, painted on the lines
But I still feel the washboard every time
It's blacktop now

[Verse 1: spoken-rap, easy flow]
Yeah, I learned to drive right here at eleven
Granddad's lap, three on the tree, felt like heaven
First beer, first kiss, first fight, first wreck
First time I cried and didn't hide it yet
Now there's a coffee drive-through where the feed store stood
A yoga place, and honestly, the coffee's pretty good
I ain't mad at the new folks, they just wanted what we had
Quiet and a sky and some room for their dad

[Chorus: sung, laid-back, nostalgic]
It's blacktop now where the dust used to rise
Streetlights shining where we counted fireflies
There's a cul-de-sac sitting on our fishing hole
They smoothed it all over, painted on the lines
But I still feel the washboard every time
It's blacktop now

[Verse 2: spoken-rap, warmer]
Got a kid on a scooter where I rode my bike
Same ditch, same hill, different kind of night
He waves, I wave, that's the same as it was
Some things don't need gravel to do what they does
My buddy sold his forty for a number with commas
Bought his mama a house, and I can't argue with mamas
So I roll through slow with the window on down
New road, old boy, same town

[Bridge: sung, band drops out]
Everything you love gets paved or grows over
You can cuss it or wave
I'm getting older. I wave.

[Final Chorus: sung, harmony above, full beat]
It's blacktop now where the dust used to rise
Streetlights shining where we counted fireflies
There's a cul-de-sac sitting on our fishing hole
They smoothed it all over, painted on the lines
But I still feel the washboard every time
It's blacktop now

[Outro: guitar, a scooter rolling past, spoken]
Evening.
Evening, sir.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 64 BPM with double-time hi-hats, 4/4, E major. Slow, wide and relaxed, a drive with one hand on the wheel.

VOICE: Male, mid-range with a Georgia-style drawl. Verses are spoken in an easy rhythm, closer to storytelling than to rap. The chorus is sung softly with a harmony above it. A boy answers him in the outro.

INSTRUMENTS: A slow strummed acoustic guitar, deep kick and a snap-like snare, quiet hi-hats, a warm sub bass, slide guitar swells, an electric guitar playing long notes in the chorus, vinyl crackle.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar and crackle. 0:12 Chorus 1. 0:42 Verse 1. 1:12 Chorus 2. 1:42 Verse 2. 2:12 Bridge, band out. 2:30 Final chorus. 3:00 Outro, a scooter and two spoken words, ends 3:18.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2010s country with a hip-hop rhythm section: roomy guitars, big soft low end, voice dry.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'I'm getting older. I wave.' at 2:24.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original celebrates the dirt road as it is. This one comes back to find it gone, and chooses not to resent the people living there now.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Loss, remembering, fairness, peace.
